headline: Wall Street's AI-driven rally is holding up despite US bond yields reaching 24-year highs, but analysts see growing risks.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: US 10-year and 30-year yields at their highest since 2002 while AI-driven earnings carry stocks.
importance_line: Anyone with a mortgage, pension or index fund is exposed to the bond-yield jump, and the AI rally now depends on big tech earnings holding up, though the article presents these as risks rather than forecasts.
summary: Bloomberg News reported on Sunday, as summarised by Seeking Alpha, that enthusiasm for AI is helping tech stocks hold up against a jump in interest rates, with the US 10-year Treasury yield above 5.3% and the 30-year at 5.69%, their highest since 2002. The summary says the Nasdaq 100 closed at a record on Friday, while strategists warn that weaker earnings or a further yield spike could expose the market's reliance on a few large technology companies.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (403); text read in a Seeking Alpha summary on TradingView (https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:46ffc30b2094b:0-ai-rally-defies-24-yr-high-in-treasury-yields-but-risks-are-building/). Original Bloomberg link kept as url. Note: C07-07 puts the S&P 500 near 1.9% below its high on 2 Oct close, this summary says "less than 1%" below the August record; the figures come from different outlets and dates.
